title: Improve streaming buffer and schema-fallback for tool-call signals
author: Amina Patel
body: Context: streaming outputs that include structured JSON (response_format) plus tool/function call signals occasionally produced interleaved or truncated JSON objects when upstream LM token pacing changed; this caused downstream JSON schema validation to fail mid-stream and broke tool-call fencing in the OpenAI compatibility layer. Motivation: improve user-visible errors, preserve partial structured payloads for debugging, and avoid silent schema corruption while keeping latency low. Summary of changes: 1) Introduces a bounded in-memory stream buffer keyed by request id that holds the most recent token window and exposes checkpoints when a tool-call start signal is observed; buffer is backpressure-aware and can drop non-structural tokens under high pressure. 2) Adds a streaming schema validator that operates incrementally: it validates at checkpoint boundaries (end-of-object, tool-call start/end) and emits structured validation hints instead of hard-failing mid-stream. 3) Implements a "toolcall-signal fence" layer in the OpenAI compat adapter that enforces that the tool/function call envelope is completed before the runtime will coerce/accept JSON payloads; if a fence breach occurs, the system produces a deterministic error event with a rehydration token for replay. 4) Improves error messages for strict mode to include validation path, offending token prefix, approximate byte offset, and a suggested fallback action (retry-with-coercion / accept-partial / escalate). 5) Adds a new opt-in runtime flag streaming_schema_mode with values permissive|checkpointed|strict to allow teams to trade strictness vs availability. 6) Adds tests, docs, and metrics for buffer drops, fence-breaches, and schema-hint triggered fallbacks. Checklist: - [x] Implementation - streaming buffer and fence layer - [x] Unit + integration tests for toolcall sequences - [x] E2E with OpenAI compatibility harness - [x] Docs + console UI hint strings - [x] Metrics and tracing spans - [x] Add changelog entry Impact: This reduces incidents where integrations observed malformed JSON during tool calls, provides clearer actionable error messages, and keeps strict mode intact by making violations explicit with deterministic replay tokens. Rollout plan: feature gated under runtime feature flag; rollout to dedicated clusters first, then gradual lift with monitoring on buffer_drop_rate and fence_breach_rate. Related work: follows up on ENG-1123 (stream resume tokens) and complements earlier schema checkpoint PRs by providing a runtime-level fence for tool calls.
commits: 3b8f2a4: add stream buffer implementation and per-request checkpoint manager
a1c4d2f: incremental schema validator with checkpoint API
d5e9b01: openai-compat adapter: add toolcall-fence and rehydrate token generation
f7e3c99: expose streaming_schema_mode flag and config parsing
c2b4a88: add unit/integration tests and fixtures for toolcall edge cases
9a7f114: docs: streaming schema mode and error message reference
bba2d33: metrics + tracing spans for buffer drops and fences
review_comments: Riley Chen: Nice approach. Can we avoid holding the full token window for very long requests? Suggest bounded LRU with eviction heuristics.
Amina Patel: Implemented a sliding-window ring buffer with a configurable max_window_bytes and LRU eviction for auxiliary metadata; added metrics for eviction_count.
Diego Morales: The rehydrate token format is sensitive. Add a short integrity checksum so we can detect accidental tampering when replaying on the client side.
Amina Patel: Added a base64url checksum field to the rehydrate token and documented the replay semantics in the OpenAI compat section.
Priya Singh: Unit tests look good; add an integration test where tool call is emitted mid-object and ensure the checkpointed validator emits a clear error and a replay token.
Amina Patel: Added e2e test (toolcall_streaming_test) that covers the mid-object tool call and asserts on the error payload shape and token replay path.
ci_summary: All CI checks passed after two reruns for flaky e2e. No remaining failures.
release_notes: Runtime: add streaming_schema_mode flag (permissive|checkpointed|strict) to control streaming JSON schema validation behavior.
Runtime: improved streaming buffer with checkpointing for tool/function call boundaries to prevent mid-stream JSON corruption.
OpenAI compat: toolcall fence and rehydrate token to allow deterministic replay after schema breaches.
Observability: new metrics buffer_drop_rate and fence_breach_rate and corresponding tracing spans.
Docs: streaming schema mode and error message guidance for operators.
tests: integration: adapter fence + rehydrate token replay
e2e: simulated LM pacing with mid-object tool call
perf: buffer heap sizing under concurrent streams
notes: This PR intentionally errs on the side of explicit failures in strict mode while offering permissive options for latency-sensitive workloads. Operators should monitor fence_breach_rate when enabling checkpointed mode.
